text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock jumped nearly 5% today, extending a two-week rally to over 18%, as oil prices spiked on escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East. News that the Trump administration is considering large-scale military operations against Iran, combined with new sanctions on Iranian tankers, sent crude prices up sharply — U.S. oil rose to $96 and global oil to $125 per barrel. For a refiner like MPC, higher crude prices tighten margins in the short term, but the stock's sustained climb suggests investors are pricing in the refiner's ability to pass costs forward and benefit from strong fuel demand amid supply concerns.

The rally has also been fueled by tight refinery conditions: U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, and both gasoline and diesel inventories are lean. This backdrop of tight supply and geopolitical risk creates an environment where refiners can maintain pricing power on the fuel they produce, offsetting the headwind of higher crude costs.
